question.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
6{x}_{2}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{2}^{2},\,4{x}_{3}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=3(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 3.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=3.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =3{x}_{1}^{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3(1)^{2}+6(0)^{2}+4(0)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $3.$
